subject: Sleep log issue preventing full analysis

messages.author: 384c8e59a54373a8
messages.subject: Sleep log issue preventing full analysis
parts:
Hi all,

I have been trying to change lines in the code according to suggestions made by several other members of this group who have run into similar sleep log issues. As I was tinkering, I realized I needed a bit more information about the way the code reads the sleep log file. For my study's screening period, some participants have one week and some have multiple weeks of sleep data but each csv file (downloaded from ActiGraph) only contains one week of sleep. 

Does the sleep log file need to be one row per week of sleep (i.e. per csv file) or should each row be one participant regardless of how many csv files that might be? I've attached screenshots of two versions of the sleep log I've tried as well as my script to make my question as clear as possible!

Further, regardless of which sleep log file I use I have received either of these error messages:

1. Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning message:
In g.loadlog(loglocation, coln1, colid, nnights, sleeplogidnum) :
  NAs introduced by coercion


2. Error in Math.factor(3L) : ‘round’ not meaningful for factors

Thank you in advance for any insight anyone can provide me.

All the best,
Sam

Hi Sam, see my responses below.

On Wednesday, May 6, 2020 8:33 PM, Samantha Scaccia <sam.s...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi all,

I have been trying to change lines in the code according to suggestions made by several other members of this group who have run into similar sleep log issues. As I was tinkering, I realized I needed a bit more information about the way the code reads the sleep log file. For my study's screening period, some participants have one week and some have multiple weeks of sleep data but each csv file (downloaded from ActiGraph) only contains one week of sleep.

> GGIR assumes one row in the sleep log file per recording.
So, I see the following solutions:
A - Thread your study phases as seperate studies. In that way ever sub-study has it's own sleeplog, where ID's in the first column match the ID of your study participants for which have a sleeplog in that study phase. Remember in the g.shell.GGIR call to specify the sleeplog file specific for that phase of the study.
B - Change the filenames to include participant ID and study phase before the first underscore, and make sure that the sleeplog file ID column refers to those new ID names that now also refer to study phase.  Next, re-process the data with argument idloc = 2, and sleeplogidnum = FALSE.

Solution A sounds the easiest to me.

Does the sleep log file need to be one row per week of sleep (i.e. per csv file) or should each row be one participant regardless of how many csv files that might be? I've attached screenshots of two versions of the sleep log I've tried as well as my script to make my question as clear as possible!
> One row per accelerometer recording. The format of the sleep log file in your screenshots looks good to me.

Further, regardless of which sleep log file I use I have received either of these error messages:

1. Error in if (WKN2 > SLN2) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning message:
In g.loadlog(loglocation, coln1, colid, nnights, sleeplogidnum) :
  NAs introduced by coercion


2. Error in Math.factor(3L) : ‘round’ not meaningful for factors
> Let me know if these errors remain after you have updated the sleep log.

Thank you in advance for any insight anyone can provide me.

All the best,
Sam

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sleep log issue preventing full analysis
parts:
GGIR generates person level estimates per average weekend day, average weekday, and across all days. With that you should be able to generate an estimate that takes into account the possible imbalance in the week- and weekend days. Further, you could set a minimum number of required nights with valid data if you are concerned that a recording is not representative. You can do this after GGIR has generated the output by removing the rows in the output that do not meet your criteria.
Best,
Vincent
